blueprint_concepts: Locus problems: midpoints of chords, feet of perpendiculars

concept_use.Parametric form of a circle: P and Q are given in parametric form (3 cos t, 3 sin t); the chord in parametric form and its x-intercept 3(1 + tan tan)/(1 - tan tan) give the fixed point (9/2, 0).
concept_use.Locus problems: midpoints of chords, fee: The midpoint M of a chord through the fixed point A satisfies OM perpendicular to MA, so M lies on the circle with OA as diameter, radius 9/4.

english: For $\theta,\phi\in(-\pi,\pi)$ with $\theta\neq\phi$, let $P=(3\cos\theta,3\sin\theta)$ and $Q=(3\cos\phi,3\sin\phi)$ be points on the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}=9$ such that $\tan\dfrac{\theta}{2}\tan\dfrac{\phi}{2}=\dfrac{1}{5}$. hindi: $\theta,\phi\in(-\pi,\pi)$, $\theta\neq\phi$ के लिए माना कि $P=(3\cos\theta,3\sin\theta)$ तथा $Q=(3\cos\phi,3\sin\phi)$ वृत्त $x^{2}+y^{2}=9$ पर ऐसे बिन्दु हैं कि $\tan\dfrac{\theta}{2}\tan\dfrac{\phi}{2}=\dfrac{1}{5}$ है। तब $PQ$ के मध्यबिन्दु का बिन्दुपथ एक वृत्त का चाप है जिसकी त्रिज्या है
solution: So every such chord passes through the fixed point $A\left(\dfrac{9}{2},0\right)$ (outside the circle)
Midpoint $M$ of a chord through $A$: $OM\perp MA$, so $M$ lies on the circle with diameter $OA$: $x^{2}+y^{2}-\dfrac{9}{2}x=0$ (only the arc inside the given circle)
solution_full: The chord joining the points with parameters $\theta$ and $\phi$ on $x^{2}+y^{2}=9$ is $x\cos\dfrac{\theta+\phi}{2}+y\sin\dfrac{\theta+\phi}{2}=3\cos\dfrac{\theta-\phi}{2}$.
Put $y=0$: the chord meets the $x$-axis at $x_{0}=\dfrac{3\cos\frac{\theta-\phi}{2}}{\cos\frac{\theta+\phi}{2}}$.

Hence $x_{0}=3\cdot\dfrac{1+\frac{1}{5}}{1-\frac{1}{5}}=3\cdot\dfrac{6}{4}=\dfrac{9}{2}$, the same for every admissible pair. So all chords $PQ$ pass through the fixed point $A\left(\dfrac{9}{2},0\right)$, which lies outside the circle since $\dfrac{9}{2}>3$.
Let $M$ be the midpoint of $PQ$. The line from the centre $O$ to the midpoint of a chord is perpendicular to the chord, so $\angle OMA=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.
Therefore $M$ lies on the circle with $OA$ as diameter: $x\left(x-\dfrac{9}{2}\right)+y^{2}=0$, i.e. $x^{2}+y^{2}-\dfrac{9}{2}x=0$.
Only the part of this circle inside $x^{2}+y^{2}=9$ is traced (the chord must cut the circle), so the locus is an arc.
originality_note: New: a parametric chord condition on the product of half-angle tangents is converted into a fixed point, and the fixed point then gives the midpoint locus (way 5, the link between the two ideas is the discovery). Closest known: chord of an ellipse with tan(a/2)tan(b/2) constant passes through a fixed point on the axis; locus of midpoints of chords through a fixed point. Different because: the fixed point is not given and must be extracted from the parametric condition before the locus can be found.
stem_review: Read as a student: every point, curve and parameter is introduced, the conditions are complete, there is one reading, the answer is unique and equals the Answer Plan, the options have one form and the Hindi mirrors the English. Added the range (-pi, pi) so the half-angle tangents exist, and theta not equal to phi so PQ is a chord. Answer 9/4 at (B) as planned. Changed: added the parameter range.
key_step: Turn the half-angle product into the fixed point (9/2, 0) through the parametric chord, then the midpoint locus is the circle on OA as diameter.
justification: Two familiar coaching results chained (parametric chord through a fixed point, midpoint locus of chords through a point); each is routine for a prepared student, so L2 rather than L3. Nearest 2026-P1-Q2 (L2); 2021-P1-Q1 (L3) needs more.
